'''''Shadows of Doubt''''' is a 2024 [[First-person (video games)|first-person]] [[Private investigator|detective]] [[Stealth game|stealth]] video game developed by British developer ColePowered Games and published by [[Fireshine Games]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Factsheet and Shadows of Doubt Description |url=http://colepowered.com/presskit/sheet.php?p=shadows_of_doubt |access-date=28 May 2023 |website=ColePowered Games}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Shadows of Doubt |url=https://www.ign.com/games/shadows-of-doubt |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427021844/https://www.ign.com/games/shadows-of-doubt |archive-date=27 April 2023 |access-date=24 April 2023 |website=[[IGN]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lawn |first=Chris |date=April 24, 2023 |title=Shadows of Doubt is one of the most astounding games of 2023 |url=https://www.gameshub.com/news/reviews/shadows-of-doubt-early-access-game-review-april-2023-2614161/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427021847/https://www.gameshub.com/news/reviews/shadows-of-doubt-early-access-game-review-april-2023-2614161/ |archive-date=27 April 2023 |access-date=24 April 2023 |website=GamesHub}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Watts |first1=Rachel |date=April 17, 2023 |title=The procedurally generated serial killer in Shadows Of Doubt is too smart for me |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/shadows-of-doubt-early-access-preview |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425180830/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/shadows-of-doubt-early-access-preview |archive-date=25 April 2023 |access-date=24 April 2023 |publisher=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]}}</ref> It was released in [[early access]] on 24 April 2023 for [[Microsoft Windows]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suther |first=Austin |date=April 21, 2023 |title=Shadows of Doubt Preview - A City at Your Fingertips |url=https://techraptor.net/gaming/previews/shadows-of-doubt-preview-city-at-your-fingertips |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230428113502/https://techraptor.net/gaming/previews/shadows-of-doubt-preview-city-at-your-fingertips |archive-date=28 April 2023 |website=TechRaptor}}</ref> Upon release, ''Shadows of Doubt'' received generally favorable views, with critics praising the innovative design of the game's open-ended gameplay, whilst critiquing its repetitive elements and bugs. The game left early access on 26 September 2024, coinciding with a digital release on [[Xbox Series S/X]] and [[PlayStation 5]], with a physical release planned in future for console versions of the game.

==Gameplay==

''Shadows of Doubt'' is an [[open world]] detective investigation game played from a [[first-person (video games)|first-person]] perspective. The player works as a private investigator who pursues murder cases in a city. The city's layout, its citizens and their routines, and all murder cases are [[procedurally-generated]] per save file, and the player can choose the city's name, size, and [[Map seed|seed]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Delaney |first=Mark |date=28 April 2023 |title=This Detective Sim Is Making Its Case As One Of The Year's Coolest Surprises |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/this-detective-sim-is-making-its-case-as-one-of-the-years-coolest-surprises/1100-6513706 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230430032643/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/this-detective-sim-is-making-its-case-as-one-of-the-years-coolest-surprises/1100-6513706/ |archive-date=30 April 2023 |access-date=2023-05-28 |website=[[GameSpot]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The player has access to police transmissions and is alerted whenever a murder is reported, allowing them to open a case. The details of each murder case are randomly configured: murders may occur anywhere and at any time, any citizen can be involved, the crime can be carried out through a variety of lethal methods, and the available [[Forensic identification|forensic evidence]] can include fingerprints, surveillance camera footage, witness observations, and more. The player also has to contend with false leads, time-sensitive evidence, anti-intrusion security measures ranging from locked doors to automated turrets, and hostile responses from citizens who catch the player doing anything illegal.

The player can complete a murder case by submitting a case resolution form to the local city hall. The form has five fields: the suspect's full name, their address, a piece of evidence placing the suspect at the crime scene, the murder weapon, and whether the suspect has been placed under arrest. Only the murderer's name is required for a successful submission, but a cash bonus is rewarded for each optional field that is correctly filled out. If the player accuses the wrong citizen, they will be fined and the real murderer will continue killing. Sometime after a murder case is resolved, the game will automatically select another citizen to carry out the next string of killings, presenting the player with a fresh case.

The player's overarching goal is to increase their social credit score by solving murder cases. Reaching the maximum social credit score enables the player to leave their city and enter retirement, concluding the game. Meanwhile, money earned from murder cases and various odd jobs is needed to purchase certain investigation tools, rent and furnish an apartment, pay for medical care when injured, pay off fines, and bribe citizens for information or access to restricted areas.

==Plot==

''Shadows of Doubt'' takes place in an [[alternate history]] that diverges from the real world in the year 1610: [[Henry IV of France]] is not assassinated, allowing English inventor [[William Lee (inventor)|William Lee's]] [[knitting machine]] to spur an early industrial revolution in France. Consequently, the [[Jacobite rising of 1745]] prevails in England and [[Charles Edward Stuart]] is crowned King Charles III, leading to lasting peace between the two countries and the subsequent formation of an [[Franco-British Union|Anglo-French Empire]] under [[Louis XVI]], which in turn quells the [[American Revolution]] in 1776. The Empire is torn apart by rebellions during the [[Mustard gas|Mustard]] War from 1891 to 1901, and then reorganized into the democratic United Atlantic States in 1902, which enshrines [[corporate personhood]] into law in order to rebuild its economy. In 1965, Starch Kola, the world's oldest [[megacorporation]], is elected President of the UAS and replaces local police forces with the privatized Starch Kola Enforcers.

The current year is 1979, and the player is a citizen of the UAS. Due to hyper-industrialization, radioactive fallout from the Mustard War, and rising sea levels caused by global warming, most people live and work in cramped, smog-shrouded cities isolated by the toxic water. Every UAS citizen dreams of attaining the lofty social credit score necessary to retire to The Fields, an exclusive district purportedly located in one of the last unsullied regions. As a former police officer, the player has the skills and tools to take on freelance investigation work. Since the Enforcers are spread thin, willing citizens are permitted to investigate murders, catalog evidence, and arrest criminals in exchange for cash and social credit score promotions. The catch is that successfully solving a murder as a freelancer often involves bending or even breaking the law.

==Development==

''Shadows of Doubt'' was created by ColePowered Games, the development studio of lead developer Cole Jeffries.<ref name=presskit>{{cite web|website=ColePowered Games|title=Shadows of Doubt: A Detective Stealth Game|accessdate=29 September 2024|url=https://colepowered.com/shadows-of-doubt/}}</ref> Jeffries began work on the game in 2018 as an [[Isometric video game graphics|isometric]] 2D [[Business simulation game|business simulation]] where players manage a detective agency to solve crimes in a city with [[procedural generation|procedurally-generated]] citizens.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2018 |title=Shadows of Doubt: A Detective Management Game! |url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-a-detective-management-game |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=Indie DB |publisher=ColePowered}}</ref> This design was later changed to a [[First-person (video games)|first-person]] 3D with players assuming the role of an individual detective, with models for the game adapted from Jeffries' 2015 city-themed title ''Concrete Jungle'' into [[pixel art]] and [[voxel|voxels]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 21, 2018 |title=Shadows of Doubt DevBlog #5 |url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-devblog-4-pivot |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=Indie DB |publisher=ColePowered}}</ref> Jeffries cited ''[[System Shock]]'' and ''[[Deus Ex (video game)|Deus Ex]]'' as inspiration for the game's first-person object interaction system,<ref>{{cite web|website=IndieDB|publisher=ColePowered|title=Shadows of Doubt DevBlog #6: First Person Adventures|date=31 July 2018|accessdate=29 September 2024|url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-devblog-6-first-person-adventures}}</ref> and the [[film noir|noir]] genre, urban landscapes of [[John Atkinson Grimshaw]] and midcentury interiors of designers including [[Verner Panton]] as references for the visual approach of the game.<ref>{{cite web|website=IndieDB|title=Shadows of Doubt DevBlog #9: Inspiration Diary|publisher=ColePowered|date=7 October 2018|accessdate=29 September 2024|url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-devblog-9-inspiration-diary}}</ref>

The [[COVID-19 pandemic]] disrupted the development schedule, although a rough playable [[Game demo|demo]] was created for the canceled [[EGX (expo)|EGX Rezzed]] expo in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 21, 2021 |title=Shadows of Doubt DevBlog #24: Roadmap 2021 |url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-devblog-24-roadmap-2021 |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=Indie DB |publisher=ColePowered}}</ref> Writer Stark Holborn was brought onto the project to flesh out the setting.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 1, 2021 |title=Shadows of Doubt DevBlog #28: Building the World Through Writing |url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-devblog-28-building-the-world-through-writing |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=Indie DB |publisher=ColePowered}}</ref>

A closed alpha test of ''Shadows of Doubt'' involving 250 participants was held in mid-2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 25, 2021 |title=Shadows of Doubt DevBlog #25: Closed Alpha Conclusions |url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-devblog-25-closed-alpha-conclusions |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=Indie DB |publisher=Colepowered}}</ref> This was followed by a public demo that was first made available during [[Steam (service)|Steam]] NextFest in February 2023, after which ColePowered Games confirmed the game's early access release date.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 27, 2023 |title=Shadows of Doubt DevBlog #32: Release Date Announce and Early Access |url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/shadows-of-doubt/news/shadows-of-doubt-devblog-32-release-date-announce-and-early-access-t |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=Indie DB |publisher=ColePowered}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Shadows of Doubt'' left early access on 26 September 2024, coinciding with a digital release on [[Xbox Series S/X]] and [[PlayStation 5]], with a physical release planned in future for console versions of the game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Romano |first=Sal |date=12 August 2024 |title=Shadows of Doubt launches September 26 |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2024/08/shadows-of-doubt-launches-september-26 |access-date=12 August 2024 |website=Gematsu}}</ref>

The game also receives future updates. On 18 September, 2025, ''Shadows of Doubt'' added new modifiers, including a mode "[[Film noir|Film Noir]]" mode with a black and white filter, [[permadeath]] and Ironman modes and a mode where the detective plays as a rat. It also added a mode titled "Snail Nemesis", apparently inspired by the "Immortal Snail" [[Internet meme|meme]] by [[Gavin Free]], in which the detective is otherwise immortal, but is stalked by a snail that kills them if it manages to catch them.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lane |first=Rick |date=September 21, 2025 |title=Shadows of Doubt's hilarious new modifiers let you play as a wall-crawling rat detective and evade a killer snail |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/sim/shadows-of-doubts-hilarious-new-modifiers-let-you-play-as-a-wall-crawling-rat-detective-and-evade-a-killer-snail/ |access-date=2025-09-22 |work=[[PC Gamer]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Reception ==

=== Pre-release ===

Describing the early access version of ''Shadows of Doubt'' as "incredibly refreshing", Rachel Watts of ''[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]'' praised the game for its "thrilling" sleuthing and advantages over scripted detective games, commending the "hands-off" design of the game in spite of its "overwhelming" pacing and investigation failures.<ref>{{cite web|website=Rock Paper Shotgun|last=Watts|first=Rachel|title=The procedurally generated serial killer in Shadows Of Doubt is too smart for me|date=24 April 2023|accessdate=12 April 2024|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/shadows-of-doubt-early-access-preview}}</ref> Zoey Handley of ''[[Destructoid]]'' found the game to have "amazing" potential, citing the game's "believable" and [[persistent world]] and "fun" casework, but noting the game's state was "pretty rough" and "can sometimes break in interesting ways and defy logic".<ref>{{cite web|website=Destructoid|title=Early Access Review: Shadows of Doubt|last=Handley|first=Zoey|date=22 April 2023|accessdate=12 April 2024|url=https://www.destructoid.com/early-access-review-shadows-of-doubt/}}</ref> Whilst praising the game's "fun" gameplay loop and "impressive" open-ended design, Liv Ngan of ''[[Eurogamer]]'' found ''Shadows of Doubt'' to be unengaging and the world to be "formulaic" due to its procedural setting, noting the game's repetitive elements, the lack of player behavior on the outcome of a case, and the inconsistent visual styles and cultures in the game's setting.<ref>{{cite web |last=Ngan |first=Liv |date=1 May 2023 |title=Shadows of Doubt is a detective game with too many threads to untangle |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/shadows-of-doubt-is-a-detective-game-with-too-many-threads-to-untangle |accessdate=12 April 2024 |website=Eurogamer}}</ref>

''Shadows of Doubt'' received "mixed or average" reviews from critics, according to review aggregator [[Metacritic]],<ref name="PC Reviews (MC)"/> and 67% of critics recommended the game, according to [[OpenCritic]].<ref name="Reviews (OC)"/> 

Reviewers generally praised the game's open-ended approach to detective gameplay, with several recounting their experiences in undertaking a complex chain of actions to complete cases.<ref name=RPS>{{cite web|website=Rock Paper Shotgun|last=Caldwell|first=Brendan|title=Shadows Of Doubt review: a buggy yet brilliant detective sim of grand ambition|date=24 September 2024|accessdate=29 September 2024|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/shadows-of-doubt-review}}</ref><ref name=PCGN/><ref name=PCG/> ''PCGamesN'' described ''Shadows of Doubt'' as one of the best detective games on PC,<ref>{{cite web|website=PCGamesN|title=The best detective games on PC 2024|last=Lees|first=Gina|date=27 September 2024|accessdate=29 September 2024|url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/best-detective-games}}</ref> with Paul Kelly writing that the game's investigation mechanics offered "complete freedom" and felt rewarding.<ref name=PCGN/> Brendan Caldwell of ''Rock Paper Shotgun'' considered the game's open-ended design lent itself to "interesting, funny, and unique-feeling" gameplay.<ref name=RPS/> Justin Wood of ''CGMagazine'' praised the investigative mechanics as a "standout feature" of the game due to the "organic and challenging" gameplay and "numerous paths for progression".<ref name=CGM/> Describing ''Shadows of Doubt'' as "one of the best mystery games ever made", Ryan Woodrow of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' praised the game as "truly unique" due to its "hands-off" gameplay, although stating that this approach could be "obtuse" and lead to "frustrating" dead ends.<ref name=SI/>

Critics expressed mixed assessments of the game's use of procedural generation in its detective gameplay. Caldwell commended the game's "commitment to simulation" and described it as a "deeply complex and [[emergent gameplay|emergent]] game", although found the "slightly wonky" behavior of characters, repetitive dialogue and case design exposed some of the "limitations of the game's world".<ref name=RPS/> Kelly stated the game's "dense sandbox" delivered on creating a "living world" with "fully-realized inhabitants", but other aspects fell short, due to the "repetitive and bland" interactions and lack of consequences to investigation.<ref name=PCGN/> Wolens expressed that many items and interactions were prone to repetition, and the generated qualities of city inhabitants lacked an organic and social element that made individuals unmemorable.<ref name=PCG/> Wood considered the game's narrative to be "engaging and vital", but noted the procedural design meant that cases lacked an "actual connective tissue" in creating a broader story.<ref name=CGM/> 

Many reviewers critiqued the persistence of technical problems in the full release of ''Shadows of Doubt''. Wolens encountered "a few technical and mechanical gripes", finding the game to be resource-intensive and the generation of larger cities to be unplayable.<ref name=PCG/> Kelly stated that unexpected and buggy behaviors from [[non-player character|NPCs]] could "break the illusion" of the simulation.<ref name=PCGN/> Wood critiqued the game's "issues and technical imperfections" on console, due to crashes, long load times, menu and cursor bugs, and errors with the behaviour of evidence that made completing cases impossible.<ref name=CGM/>
